title: Pseudo-Elias of Cortona, Lumen luminum, cipher recipes and zodiac table, North Italy c. 1525 (Beinecke Mellon MS 29; DECODE R2877)

documents.shelfmark: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Mellon MS 29, ff. 1v-2v and front pastedown; DECODE R2877

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the manuscript (the later pastedown copy is unglossed), in the Beinecke catalogue, in Rec 2014 or in Galiano's articles.

transcription.source: Yale Digital Collections IIIF, canvases 17388795-17388799 (full resolution crops)
transcription.notes: Sol recipe list (f. 1v), Luna recipe list (f. 2r) and 12-entry zodiac table (f. 2v); q/g distinction uncertain (Rec 2014 reads g where this transcription has q in two entries). Scribal signs kept as 3 (ʒ), 7 (et-sign), 9 (con-sign), B (ß). The pastedown copy is recorded but not counted. 'in' and 'cioe' are clear words inside the f. 2r list and are included in the count.

system.summary: Letter strings with a few scribal signs, standing for the substances behind twelve zodiac cover names and for two recipe lists; not simple substitution, possibly polyalphabetic, a whole-name code, or invented pseudo-text.

prior_solution.where: DECODE R2877 Non-decrypted; Rec 2014 (Societas Magica Newsletter 31, n. 8) calls it a code and does not solve it

conditions.human_role: Selected the target from the catalogue and set the goal; no other input.

solution.what: Downloaded all 69 Yale IIIF images of Mellon MS 29 and full-resolution crops of the cipher lines; checked DECODE R2877 (same images, no transcription, no key).
Beinecke catalogue description, Rec 2014 (Societas Magica Newsletter 31), Galiano's articles on Elias' alchemical codices, general web search for the Italian prologue.
Located the cipher (ff. 1v, 2r, 2v and the pastedown copy; ff. 3r-37v checked, clear) and transcribed the 234-letter corpus with its scribal signs.

IC 0.075 in both sections (language-like), but the zodiac table and the recipe lists have different letter profiles (q 17% vs <2%, h 3% vs 10%); Sukhotin puts q as the main vowel in one and r in the other.
One-to-one monoalphabetic annealing against Italian and Latin, with and without word division, q/g split and merged, sections together and apart: best -4.0 per char (gibberish).
A synthetic 206-letter Italian ingredient list under a random key is recovered by the same solver at -2.6 per char, so a simple substitution of Italian would have been found.
Homophonic (many-to-one) annealing; Caesar and Trithemius progressive shifts per entry over five alphabets; Vigenere periods 2-7 restarting or running; reversed words; alternate-letter nulls.

Alberti cipher disk (lowercase ring with k, y, h, &; capitals R and V inside the runs as index letters): Alberti's published ring per segment, then an unknown ring with 19 per-segment offsets annealed jointly.
Word-pattern solver over ~170 Italian substance, number and weight words: no consistent key; Virgo 'pqyqpqsqst' and the 'qrqr'/'lrqrlr' shapes fit no substance name.

outcome.fraction_read_source: ciphertext.txt: no letter given a value
outcome.notes: Attempted, closed unread. Not a letter: an alchemical codex; the cipher hides the substances behind twelve zodiac cover names and two recipe lists. Not simple substitution; no key, clear copy or print decipherment known; possibly invented pseudo-text (the Beinecke catalogue's 'hint of charlatanism').

gaps.detail: not simple substitution; no key or clear copy known

gaps.item: Sol and Luna recipe lists, ff. 1v and 2r
gaps.detail: about 115 letters, too short for a polyalphabetic attack without a key
